agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:157:**How tools are loaded for now.** Both adapters load every registered tool on every turn. The in-app adapter sends the full function list with each request, and MCP `tools/list` returns the whole catalog. This is the simplest behaviour that is correct. It also keeps the tools array byte-identical through a chat, and OpenAI's prompt cache depends on exactly that. The budget is 20 definitions per turn. Going over 20 does not block anything. It is the point at which we start watching the measurements. The live regression test records definition bytes, input tokens, and cached tokens for each request. The journey catalog below goes over 20 definitions from its first milestone. We accept that until those measurements show the model selecting wrong tools or running short of context.

content.content:
## Skills versus tools

A skill is text the model reads. A tool is something the app executes. To decide which one a candidate is, ask one question: does it have to run, or does it only have to be read?

- It has to run if it reads state the model does not have, computes something only OrcaSlicer can compute, or changes the project. That makes it a tool.
- It only has to be read if it is judgement, the order to do things in, facts about printing, how to interpret a tool's result, or which question to ask first. That makes it a skill.

The section above covers tools. This section covers skills, and decides the cases that fall in between.

A skill contains things the model could do by itself if it had the right knowledge. It contains nothing that executes. Examples:

- judging evidence, such as telling an adhesion failure from wet filament in a photo;
- the order of a series of tool calls, and the reasons for that order. For "make it stronger": read the settings, change walls and infill, slice, read the report;
- facts about printing, such as what PETG tolerates;
- which question to ask when the answer would change the plan.

A skill is a file on the Agent page, `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: frontmatter with its `name` and a `trigger`, a `description` or both, then the text the model gets. The page sends every skill once per connection with the `skills` bridge message. A skill with a trigger is the app's: when the event it names happens, the host adds it to the one request where the model first reads about the event, as the request's last item, and to no later request. A skill with a description is the model's: `skill_read` lists the described skills in its own description and returns one by name, and is offered only while at least one exists. One skill has a description and a trigger: `calibration`, read when a print problem may come from the filament or its settings, when the person asks to calibrate, or in a calibration project, and fired by `calibration_started` on the first turn of a calibration project's chat; it carries the conversation of a calibration (when a test is worth it, the two facts said before the person's project closes, asking which test only when the handover leaves it open, per-test ranges and how to read the print, the naming rule for the saved preset), while `calibration_generate`'s description keeps only that tool's rules. Four other skills have triggers, one file each:

- `file-loaded` (trigger `file_loaded`): the first message after a file is opened or imported is a judgement about the load report. It fires when the person opens or drops a file, after an in-app `object_import` (and a failed `project_open`) in the same turn, and in the opened project's chat after an in-app `project_open`, which replaces the conversation and so ends the turn that asked. An MCP client's loads fire nothing. The host sends a picture of the active plate with it and, when no purpose is recorded, one sentence of its own built from that state.
- `project-setup-changed` (trigger `setup_changed`): check the setup in force against the print's purpose. It fires on the result of an in-app `setup_record` that recorded a purpose for the first time or changed it (its result says which in `purposeChange`; a call that restates the same purpose, or leaves it out, to change the plan does not fire it), when the printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the setup the model was last asked to check under a recorded purpose (on the next tool result of the turn, or on the next turn's first request when the person changed it by hand), on a turn's first request after the person restored an earlier version while a purpose is recorded, and on every turn's first request while the plan is marked `needs_reassessment` (2026-10-28: the model may leave recording the plan to the turn that answers its question about the change, and that turn finds the setup checked already, so without this the mark could outlive every skill that explains it). Each time the model is asked to check, the app saves the setup in force as the one checked. The model's own successful `printer_setup` fires nothing: the setup it chose is saved as checked at once (Kenneth, 2026-10-19), so the skill is for a setup that moved without the model, and a pairing its change breaks is caught by the slice-refusal facts and skill. It gives way to the file-loaded skill on a request that carries both, since that skill already asks for the same check.
- `slice-failed` (trigger `slice_failed`): a plate's last slice did not succeed, because OrcaSlicer's check refused the plate or the run failed. The adapter records why on the plate (`WorkspacePlate::slice_failure`: refused or failed, OrcaSlicer's words, the setting and object when named) at the moment it happens (a hook in `Plater::reslice`, `Workspace/SliceRequests.hpp`, and the run's completion event), worded by the print-issue monitor's `slice_failure_of`, and keeps it until the plate slices. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceFailure`; `slice_report` of an unsliced plate adds the check code and the object's name. The skill fires once per failure, on the first request that carries it: the result of the model's own `slice_start`, the turn the app starts when a slice the model started fails after its turn, or the next message after the person's Slice all. The same refusal again is the same failure.
- `print-issues` (trigger `print_issues`): what the print-issue chip's Ask AI button asks for and how to read what OrcaSlicer reports. The adapter reads a slice's warnings through the monitor's `slice_warnings_of` while the plate is active and keeps a summary on the plate while that slice is current (`WorkspacePlate::slice_warnings`: the count, how many the person ignored, and the first warning, critical first, in OrcaSlicer's words with its setting and object). It counts every warning the chip lists. The chip and `slice_report` read the same slice-result rule (`Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`), so they list the same warnings, except that `slice_report` also lists the timelapse ones, marked `appliesWhen: "timelapse"`, which the chip does not count. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceWarnings`. The skill fires on the request that carries a chip's message, and on the first request whose workspace shows warnings no request has carried yet, whether the person sliced (their next message) or the model did (the tool result that shows them, or the app's turn when its slice ended after its turn); a re-slice with the same warnings fires nothing.

The connection skills (`connect-bambu`, and `connect-print-host` for every print host type) have rules of their own, in [Writing a connection skill](connection-skill-guide.md).

The cases in between:

- **A procedure made of existing tool calls.** It is a skill for as long as carrying it out takes judgement. It becomes a tool only when the steps are fixed and the person wants the whole thing as one action that can be undone. If there are many such fixed sequences, they go in one workflow registry (see [When resources or skills are appropriate](#when-resources-or-skills-are-appropriate)).
- **An analysis.** It is a tool when OrcaSlicer computes it and always gets the same answer, such as overhang angles from geometry. It is a skill when it is a judgement about evidence. Pair that skill with the tool that supplies the evidence (`view_render`, `slice_report`).
- **Large reference data.** When the model needs only one part of the data, make it a tool that returns the part an argument selects, as `settings_search` does. When the model needs to see all of the data before it can use any of it, make it text. The printer list described under [Input design](#input-design) is the case we measured: putting the whole list in the instructions worked better than the search tool.
- **A tool description versus a skill.** A tool description says when to call that one tool, in the words a person would use. A skill says how several tools fit together and what to conclude from their results. If a tool description has grown into a step-by-step procedure, move the procedure out into a skill.

When you are not sure, start with a skill. A skill is a text file that ships with the page. A tool costs the whole implementation sequence described below, including fakes, tests, and rebase evidence. Turn a skill into a tool only on the kind of evidence every tool starts from (see [Start with an eval failure](#start-with-an-eval-failure)). Either transcripts show the model getting the sequence wrong in ways that better text does not fix, or the action needs something only the app can give: all-or-nothing application, validation, or undo. The opposite sign exists too. If a skill has turned into exact values and calls in a fixed order, with no judgement between them, it should be written as a tool.

How something gets loaded into the model's context does not decide whether it is a skill or a tool. Today a skill costs its one line in the instructions, and a tool costs its definition on the first request of a conversation (see [Tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)). If we later use the model platform's deferred loading, both will cost one index line plus a load when needed. A skill could then be a deferred read-only tool: the tool's description is the skill's index line, and the tool's result is the skill's text. Tools and skills would then be found the same way and covered by the same eval.

## When resources or skills are appropriate

Do not make anything depend on MCP resources until the clients we intend to support have shown that their models fetch resources reliably. A tool that returns a size-limited amount of data is what every client can be expected to handle. Resources may be added as an optional second way to get data that is large, readable, and stable.

Keep printing playbooks as skills the model can read (see [Skills versus tools](#skills-versus-tools)). Examples are reducing stringing, improving strength, and choosing a support strategy. Turn a workflow into an executable tool only when it corresponds to a named OrcaSlicer operation that always behaves the same way and has defined inputs, outputs, validation, and behavior for undo, reset, and cancellation. If many step-by-step workflows eventually qualify, build one workflow registry that the model can search, in preference to dozens of nearly identical tool definitions.

agent-docs/jusprin/connection-skill-guide.md:35:Kenneth, 2026-11-02: for each failure, is the cause a lack or wrong *information* (a fact about this situation that only the app can know at that moment) or a lack or wrong *knowledge* (how things work)? agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:258:- **Undo.** None of this state is in OrcaSlicer's undo stack. Results say `projectUndo: false`. Region annotations are the awkward case. They generate OrcaSlicer artifacts (modifier volumes, enforcers, blockers, paint), and those artifacts *are* in the undo stack. So project Undo can leave an annotation without its artifacts, or leave an artifact without its annotation. - **Being asked for a credential they do not have.** A Klipper owner who has never heard of an API key; a Bambu owner who cannot find the access code. The skill says, in order of cost to check, what is likeliest and what they can look at, each labelled as observed, documented or a guess. The 401-without-a-key case was the one place both 2026-11-04 Moonraker runs got stuck, when the skill had only "search for where their version shows it".
- **Being told it is connected.** What the app's test proved and did not prove, so the closing sentence does not promise what the app has not checked.

For each moment, write what a competent friend would say to someone standing at that screen. That sentence is the skill's job; the failure table supports it.

### 2. Information against knowledge, per state

Kenneth, 2026-11-02: for each failure, is the cause a lack or wrong *information* (a fact about this situation that only the app can know at that moment) or a lack or wrong *knowledge* (how things work)? Information belongs in the app's note or tool result; knowledge about connecting belongs in the skill; how to work in general belongs in the prompt.

Before writing a line of the skill, list the app's notes and tool results for this connection type and, for each, what the app already holds at that moment that the model would need. Where the result lacks it, the fix is to the result, and the skill is written against the result that will exist. Two gaps found this way on 2026-11-04 are fixed: the Moonraker result now says which key each test sent (none, the one typed in the form, or the saved one), and the verified result gives Klipper's state, which the app read and had only logged.

"Already holds" is the limit. A result forwards what the code has; it does not gain a new probe to tell causes apart ([How to fix a result that hides the failure](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#how-to-fix-a-result-that-hides-the-failure), rule 2). After 2026-11-02 the Bambu failure note gained a look at the printer's port 8883 before and after each attempt, and the skill gained four cases built on what the port did. The failures it was built to explain came from a development build with Enable SSL(MQTT) off (see [Three kinds of statement](#three-kinds-of-statement-each-labelled)), and both were removed on 2026-11-16.

### 3. The standing prompt and the tool descriptions

List every sentence in `printerInstructions.ts` and in the connection tools' descriptions (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`) that gives an exact wording, an exact step or a procedure for connecting. Each one either goes, becomes conditional, or is accepted knowing the skill cannot override it. On 2026-11-04 four such sentences caused failures the skill's facts should have prevented, and all four have since been removed: the exact offer after `printer_add` (asked a person who had already asked to connect), "say briefly to use that form" after a key was requested (told a person with no key to type one), the finishing example above, and the connect tool's "until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this" (made the model ask permission to try a port the person had just said to try).

This matches [Tool extension guide, A tool description versus a skill](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#skills-versus-tools): a description that has grown into a step belongs in the skill. The skill work had added new text without sweeping the old. **Proposed:** the sweep is a required step of every connection skill change.

## Writing the skill

### Explain the mechanism as a chain

Number the steps the connection goes through, each depending on the one before, and say so: a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it. This is what let the model reason about failures the skill did not list on 2026-11-03 (an OctoPrint the person called Klipper; `https://` against a plain-http host). Keep the chain from the person's side as well as the app's: for Moonraker, the app reaches Moonraker at its port, and so does the person's browser, so Moonraker's own pages are at that same address and port. A skill that explained only the app's side sent the person to a port-80 URL for the key (2026-11-04).

### Three kinds of statement, each labelled

- **Observed on a real host or printer.** What the app's own test reported, and when. The guard tests in `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` require every state the skill names in backquotes to have a dated run behind it. Write these as facts.
- **Documented.** What a maintainer's docs or FAQ say, named ("Mainsail's FAQ for this error says…"). Write these with their source. The evidence rule does not forbid them; leaving them out is what made the host skills silent about the one thing a stuck Klipper owner needs (a 401 from a printer on the same home network is usually fixed in Moonraker's `trusted_clients`, with no key at all).
- **A guess.** General knowledge nobody has checked on this setup. Write it as a guess and give the cheapest check.

An observation counts only from an app set up the way people get it. Every "real P1S" result before 2026-11-04 came from a development build with Enable SSL(MQTT) off in the app's settings, which logs in to the printer without TLS: code -1 with the right access code, and a failure about 24 seconds after the attempt began. A release build takes TLS from the printer, and with the setting on the same P1S connected in about a second. The skill, its guard and the prompt cases stated those artifacts as facts for two weeks. **Proposed:** before a run on a real printer is recorded as observed, the record says which build ran it and, for a development build, the settings that differ from a release build.

content.text:
You're right that the app's note is the place for this, but printers have no similar text. A filament switch from the header posts that note line; a printer switch from the header posts nothing. Changing the wording would cover the filament case only, and the printer case needs a new note.

**The doc you mean.** It is `agent-docs/jusprin/connection-skill-guide.md`, section "Information against knowledge, per state", which records your rule from 2026-11-02:

> Information belongs in the app's note or tool result; knowledge about connecting belongs in the skill; how to work in general belongs in the prompt.

"Your change to the nozzle temperature was not carried over" is information: a fact about this moment that only the app knows. That makes the app's note the right home, not the prompt. Your 2026-10-17 rule says the same, that the standing prompt holds principles and everything situational comes from the app when it applies. That rule is in my notes; I found no committed copy apart from the connection guide.

**What the code does today:**
- **Filament switch from the header:** `StatusRow::on_filament_visit` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp` posts the line when the menu closes: "Filament is now Generic PLA. Heat and cooling follow PLA; walls and infill unchanged. Slice again when ready." That is the text the code builds, not a captured run. The model gets it as a developer message.
- **Printer switch from the header:** `StatusRow::open_printer_menu` passes the printer menu no way to post a note, and the printer menu posts none itself. The model sees only the new name in the workspace tag.

**Proposed, not agreed:**
- **Filament note:** after the existing text, add a sentence naming what was dropped, for example: "Unsaved changes to Bambu PLA Basic were not carried over: nozzle temperature is back to 220 °C."
- **New printer note:** a matching line posted from the printer menu, naming the new printer and the changes it dropped.

Three things to know first:
- **The person sees the same text.** You decided on 2026-10-28 that the model reads the very line the person sees. So this is on-screen wording, and per the design guidelines it needs a whole-screen design board and a cold-reader check before it is built.
- **The app has to keep the list itself.** OrcaSlicer can list which settings were unsaved (`PresetCollection::current_dirty_options`), but only before the switch drops them. The note is built after the menu closes, so the switch has to keep that list.
- **What each switch drops differs.** A printer switch drops unsaved changes in the printer, filament and process profiles. A filament switch drops only the filament's. Each note should name only what its switch dropped.

I changed nothing. If you want the proposal, the next step is a design board with both lines in their real place in the chat.

Agreed, a fixed sentence is enough. To answer your question: the version I proposed would have had to list every dropped setting, so the note could name nozzle temperature and its new value. That meant keeping the list before the switch, so it was more machinery than the problem needs.

**Proposed, not agreed:** one fixed sentence added to each note, with no list. If it says "any unsaved changes", it is true whether or not anything was dropped. So the app doesn't even need to know whether there were changes, and the note needs no new information.

- **Filament note, the existing line plus one sentence:** "Filament is now Generic PLA. Any unsaved setting changes were dropped; settings now follow the Generic PLA profile. Slice again when ready."
  - "Heat and cooling follow PLA; walls and infill unchanged" overlaps with the new sentence, so I'd drop it.
  - One detail to keep accurate: a filament switch drops only the filament's own unsaved changes. Walls and infill changes survive it, as in the test where wall loops stayed at 5. So the sentence should not suggest that every setting went back.
- **Printer note, new because the printer menu posts none today:** "Printer is now Second printer. Any unsaved setting changes were dropped; settings now follow the profiles of Second printer."
  - A printer switch drops unsaved changes in the printer, filament and process profiles, so here "settings" can mean all of them.

# JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

```bash
python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py
```

It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the
pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new
entry in every `<lang>.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's
`AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line
break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine
translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: <what>` where
the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails
while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder.

The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like
`<0>…</0>` for elements inside a `Trans`, and
`{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the
placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a
plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses
(`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`).

## Marking text

Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items,
tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error
text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly
as it was.

Leave these in English, unmarked:

- **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool
  results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a
  request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and
  `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the
  person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown.
- Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes,
  test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code.
- Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`,
  `report_error`): they are read by developers.
- Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect JusPrin's own interface text into its translation catalogs.

JusPrin keeps its translations apart from OrcaSlicer's, so taking a new
OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a catalog:

  * native/JusPrin.pot and native/<lang>.po hold the text the native windows
    mark with _L, _u8L, L, _L_CONTEXT and _L_PLURAL under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin.
    Text OrcaSlicer's own template already has is left out: its translations
    come from upstream. Brand/brand_catalogs.py merges these into the catalog
    the app loads.
  * pages/<lang>.po hold the text of the AI and Home pages, marked with the
    Lingui macros (t, Trans, Plural). Lingui's own extractor writes them.

Run it after marking or changing text, then translate the new entries:

    python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

Needs GNU gettext (xgettext, msgmerge, msgcat, msgcomm) and the pages'
node_modules (npm ci in AgentUI).
"""

import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
JUSPRIN = HERE.parent
ROOT = JUSPRIN.parents[3]
UPSTREAM_I18N = ROOT / "localization" / "i18n"
NATIVE = HERE / "native"
PAGES = HERE / "pages"

# The keywords upstream's scripts/run_gettext.sh passes, and
# translated_plural from Support/Translate.hpp.
XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS = [
    "--keyword=L", "--keyword=_L", "--keyword=_u8L",
    "--keyword=L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_u8L_CONTEXT:1,2c",
    "--keyword=_L_PLURAL:1,2", "--keyword=translated_plural:1,2",
]
# Test doubles and the page projects are not native interface text.
SKIP_DIRS = {"Testing", "AgentUI", "HomeUI", "WebShared", "node_modules", "Localization"}

DATE = re.compile(r'^"POT-Creation-Date: .*\\n"\n', re.M)


def languages():
    data = json.loads((HERE / "languages.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [l["code"] for l in data["languages"] if l["code"] != data["source"]]


def run(*args, **kw):
    subprocess.run(list(args), check=True, **kw)


def keep_if_only_date_changed(path, before):

# OrcaSlicer's messages in the JusPrin view

OrcaSlicer tells the person things in windows: a box with OK, a question, the
"Transfer or discard changes" window, a tip. In the JusPrin view most of those
windows would cover a screen built around the project chat, and many of them
are about pages the view hides. JusPrin takes each such message before its
window opens, keeps the reason it was said, and shows it where the view shows
that kind of news. The code is in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/OrcaMessages/`.

## Where a message is taken

OrcaSlicer speaks in one of two ways.

- It opens a modal window inside the call that decided to speak. Every modal
  window passes wxWidgets' modal hook, where JusPrin's dialog listeners
  already answer the windows a tool call or a file open raises
  (`Workspace/DialogListeners.hpp`). A window no listener answered goes to
  `OrcaMessages::take_modal`, while the code that asked is still on the stack.
- It puts the message off. `GUI::show_error`, `GUI_App::show_dialog` and
  `GUI_App::push_notification` queue the window and return, so by the time it
  opens the reason is gone. One line at the top of each of the three functions
  hands the message over first: `report_error_box` (`Workspace/FileLoads.hpp`),
  `take_app_message` and `take_printer_message`. A fourth line in
  `GUI_App::process_network_msg` notes that what follows is the network
  plug-in's message. The lines reach JusPrin through `JusPrin/OrcaHooks.hpp`.

Those four lines are the fork's whole footprint in OrcaSlicer's files for this
feature. Each is one neutral statement marked `// JusPrin:`.

## The cause

A message is only as useful as its reason. The reason, a `Cause`, is noted at
the doors where work comes in, by code that knows it:

| Cause | Noted by |
| --- | --- |
| A printer's answer to a connection | `Printers::record_connection_event`, called from OrcaSlicer's connection handler before it opens its box |
| A printer's reply to a command | `take_printer_message`, which `push_notification` gives the printer |
| The network plug-in's message | `plugin_message_cause`, at the top of `process_network_msg` |
| A slice that ended in an error | JusPrin's listener of the finished slice, which runs before OrcaSlicer's |
| A failed upload to a print host | JusPrin's listener of the upload queue's error event, which notes the words of the upload's notification |

A cause noted by a listener lasts until the event being handled ends
(`note_cause`); one noted by a scope lasts while the scope does
(`ScopedCause`). A person's click in OrcaSlicer's own menus has no cause.

A cause can say that the code that noted it tells the person itself
(`told_elsewhere`): the print issues tell a failed slice, and the printer chat
tells the answer to a connection it started and is waiting for
(`Printers::expect_connection_answer`). Such a message is taken and shown
nowhere else, so the person does not read it twice.

## The rule at the hook

For a window no listener answered, while the view is installed:

- A file or folder picker and the chooser of a ZIP's files are the person's and
  open as OrcaSlicer's. A listener of a file the person opens themself shows
  them too, rather than cancelling them.
- A window with fields, and a question with more than one answer, are the
  person's and open.
- A message with only OK is taken, unless another window is open over the main
  one, such as OrcaSlicer's settings window or Preferences, and the message has
  no cause. The box then belongs with that window, where the person is
  looking.
- "Transfer or discard changes", and the "unsaved changes" question OrcaSlicer
  asks before it reloads profiles (`check_and_save_current_preset_changes`,
  `check_and_keep_current_preset_changes`), are answered after a version of
  the project is saved to its history: the setting changes are dropped and
  the version keeps them. The person never chooses between saving and
  discarding; version history is the way back. If no version can be saved,
  the window is cancelled, so nothing changes, and the failure is reported as
  an unexpected error. Closing the project follows the same rule through the
  same function, `ShellController::save_before_dropping_changes`, which
  Plater's hook before a project is released also calls: whenever OrcaSlicer
  is about to drop setting changes that sit on a profile, a version is saved
  first, or nothing is dropped and nothing closes. Restoring that version
  from Version history brings back the profiles, their unsaved changes and
  the model as they were just before.
- The version must hold the project as it was before the switch began, not
  halfway through it. A filament switch runs the sidebar's sequence
  (`SetupCommands::select_filament_preset`), which renames the filament slot
  before OrcaSlicer asks, so a version saved at the question would name the
  new filament with the old one's settings. That switch saves first itself,
  before the slot changes (`OrcaMessages::SavedFirst`), and the question that
  follows is answered without saving again. The printer and process switches
  ask before they change anything.
- The same window class asks whether to copy one nozzle's settings to the
  other on a two-nozzle printer (`Tab::sync_excluder`). That is a question
  about a copy and stays the person's. OrcaSlicer tells the three uses apart
  only by their titles, so JusPrin compares the titles as OrcaSlicer builds
  them.
- A tip window is taken.
- JusPrin's own windows are never taken. They open through
  `OrcaMessages/OwnDialogs.hpp` (`show_own_modal`, `show_own_message`,
  `show_own_error`), which marks them as JusPrin's while they are shown.

The view also refuses a switch of the main window to any page other than Home,
Prepare and Project (`ShellController::on_notebook_page_changing`), so code
that jumps to OrcaSlicer's Device page, or the key that steps through its
pages, leaves the person where they are.

## Where a taken message is shown

Every taken message that is not told elsewhere goes into the project chat,
the same way for every cause (`OrcaMessages/MessageRoutes.hpp`). If a chat is
open the entry is added to it; otherwise it starts the chat, which is what
the empty chat panel shows. The entry is the kind the app's own work leaves
there (`Agent::AgentHost::begin_work`), marked failed and carrying
OrcaSlicer's words; the chat card shows an entry's words only in that state.
The chat pane opens for it. The entry is saved with the project, so a message
that comes while the person is on Home, where the chat pane is not shown, is
in the chat when they open the project.

- A message about a printer, a connection's answer or a command's reply, is
  titled with the printer's name as JusPrin names it.
- A failed upload to a print host ends the upload's own entry as failed,
  rather than adding a second one.
- Any other message is titled as OrcaSlicer's window would have been: "Info"
  for `GUI_App::show_dialog`, "<app> error" for `GUI::show_error`, the box's
  own title for a modal box.
- A message told elsewhere, an answered unsaved-changes question, a tip, a
  refused page switch: nothing more.

Nothing taken is drawn on the canvas. The words are OrcaSlicer's, unchanged
and translated by its catalogs.

## Testing

`JusPrinShellHarness --orca-messages <dir>` makes OrcaSlicer speak through
its real code in each of these ways and checks which window opened, what was
taken with which cause, and where it was shown. `--classic-messages` turns the
taking off while the view stays installed (`set_taking_for_tests`), so the same
run shows OrcaSlicer's windows as the classic view does. Every harness mode
fails its run if, while the view takes messages, an OrcaSlicer message with
only OK or an unsaved-changes question reached the person, or a printer
message was taken without its printer.

content.text:
Commit `3efec304d4` on `claude/orca-messages-c67fbe` makes both header switches post a chat line saying the unsaved changes were dropped. The model gets that line on its next request, and in the retest every answer that came back said the switch dropped the change. Nothing is merged or pushed.

**What the person and the model now see:**
- **Printer switch from the header:** "Printer is now Second printer. Any unsaved setting changes were dropped; the settings now follow the newly selected printer, filament and process profiles. Slice again when ready." The printer menu posted nothing before.
- **Filament switch from the header:** "Filament is now Generic PLA. Any unsaved filament setting changes were dropped; the filament settings now follow the Generic PLA profile. Slice again when ready." The new sentence replaces "Heat and cooling follow PLA; walls and infill unchanged."

The filament line says "filament setting changes" because a filament switch drops only the filament's own changes. A wall-loops change survives it, as the test showed.

**One extra fix:** the model now gets these lines in English while the chat shows them in the person's language. Before, the model got them translated, which the localization README says not to do. The new strings are in all 22 of JusPrin's catalogs, marked as AI translated.

**Tests:**
- **Harness checks:** the printer-menu mode checks the printer line and the default mode checks the filament line. Both pass.
- **Recorder:** it now switches by pressing the real header menu rows, so the app posts each line itself. The recorded request ends with the line as a developer message.
- **Model batch:** the same batch as before, DeepSeek V4 Flash, 3 runs of the printer case and 3 of the temperature case. Five of six runs came back with an answer, and each said the switch dropped the change. For example: "No — the switch to the second printer dropped the unsaved setting, so wall loops are back to 2." The sixth asked for settings the recording had no answer for. Before the fix the model found the lower value by reading the setting and guessed at the cause ("probably when the printer preset was switched"). The batch was 12 requests, 168,339 input tokens (89,344 cached) and 3,266 output tokens, about the same cost as last time.
- **Other checks:** clang-tidy and the catalog test pass.

**Still open:**
- **Not tested in another language.** A translated run, where the chat and the model get different text, was not run.
- **The model sometimes acts without asking.** In one printer-switch run it started putting wall loops back to 5 and raising infill to 25% straight away. The recording stops there, so whether it would apply that without asking the person is unknown.
- **A test commit I didn't write.** `b8f6c163fa`, which made the recorder post the filament line, appeared on this branch while I worked, under your name. Its two files had been reset in the working copy, so I restored them from that commit and then built on it.
